content: Each interaction is described in detail, as requested: 1. Amphotericin B Liposomal and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination may also elevate tenofovir levels. 2. Amphotericin B Phospholipid Complex and Tenofovir DF: Similar to the liposomal formulation, this combination increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Monitor closely and use caution. Tenofovir levels may also rise. 3. Anastrozole and Doravirine: Anastrozole increases doravirine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 4. Apalutamide and Doravirine: Apalutamide decreases doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for reduced efficacy and virologic failure. 5. Apalutamide and Tenofovir DF: Apalutamide increases the elimination of tenofovir DF, reducing its levels or effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Apalutamide weakly induces BCRP, potentially decreasing systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. 6. Armodafinil and Doravirine: Armodafinil reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 7. Atazanavir and Doravirine: Atazanavir increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Atazanavir and Lamivudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 9. Atazanavir and Tenofovir DF: This combination increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tenofovir DF decreases atazanavir levels through an unknown mechanism, potentially reducing its antiviral activity. Ritonavir boosting may help compensate. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Tenofovir DF and Bacitracin: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid concurrent use of bacitracin with other nephrotoxic drugs. Monitor closely. 11. Belzutifan and Doravirine: Belzutifan reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of doravirine and monitor closely. 12. Berotralstat and Tenofovir DF: Berotralstat increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of P-gp substrates if coadministered. 13. Betibeglogene Autotemcel and Antiretroviral Therapy (ART): ART medications may interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. Avoid ART for at least one month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 14. Bexarotene and Doravirine: Bexarotene reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 15. Black Cohosh and Tenofovir DF: This combination may increase toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, with a potential risk of hepatotoxicity. Monitor closely. 16. Bleomycin and Tenofovir DF: Bleomycin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Bosentan and Doravirine: Bosentan reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 18. Brigatinib and Doravirine: Brigatinib reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 19. Butabarbital and Doravirine: Butabarbital reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 20. Cabozantinib and Lamivudine: Lamivudine increases cabozantinib levels or effects by inhibiting MRP2. Use caution and monitor closely for toxicity. 21. Capreomycin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Carbamazepine and Doravirine: Carbamazepine reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 23. Carboplatin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. This combination may also elevate tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Celecoxib and Tenofovir DF: Celecoxib increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely to avoid toxicity. 25. Cenobamate and Doravirine: Cenobamate reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of doravirine as needed and monitor closely. 26. Ceritinib and Doravirine: Ceritinib increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Chloramphenicol and Doravirine: Chloramphenicol increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Cisplatin and Tenofovir DF: Cisplatin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination, potentially increasing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Clarithromycin and Doravirine: Clarithromycin increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Clobazam and Doravirine: Clobazam reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 31. Cobicistat and Doravirine: Cobicistat increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Colistin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Conivaptan and Doravirine: Conivaptan increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Contrast Media (Iodinated) and Tenofovir DF: Both agents increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 35. Cyclophosphamide and Doravirine: Cyclophosphamide increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 36. Cyclosporine and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Dabigatran and Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir DF reduces dabigatran levels or effects by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration. 38. Dabrafenib and Doravirine: Dabrafenib reduces doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 39. Danazol and Doravirine: Danazol increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 40. Danicopan and Tenofovir DF: Danicopan increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Darolutamide and Tenofovir DF: Darolutamide increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting BCRP. Avoid coadministration with BCRP inhibitors. If unavoidable, monitor closely and consider dose reduction. 42. Darunavir and Doravirine: Darunavir increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Dichlorphenamide and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Diclofenac and Tenofovir DF: Diclofenac increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 45. Didanosine and Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir DF increases didanosine toxicity by reducing elimination. Adjust didanosine dose and monitor closely for pancreatitis risk. 46. Diflunisal and Tenofovir DF: Diflunisal increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Digoxin and Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir DF increases digoxin levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Dofetilide and Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir DF increases dofetilide levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Drospirenone and Doravirine: Drospirenone increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 50. Duvelisib and Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir DF reduces duvelisib levels or effects by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. This list continues with similar detailed descriptions for each drug interaction.
